name: Newcomen atmospheric pumping engine
summary: Newcomen's engine condensed steam under a piston so air pressure pushed it down, working a beam that pumped water out of mines.
description: Steam condensation creates a pressure difference that drives a piston and beam for mine pumping in the Newcomen atmospheric arrangement.
tier_reason: The practical engine architecture supports successive mining, power and steam-engine developments rather than only a later surviving museum specimen.

impact.note: Working power from steam drained mines across Britain and Europe and the steam engine line grew from it; importance.md anchors generativity at 2, implying tier 1 not 0.

why: Deepening British coal and metal mines were flooding, and coal to fuel an engine was cheap at the pithead.
